videos.t: Rotary Cell Phone Prototype

An artifact from somewhere else.

Want to buy me a coffee? Your tips support more videos like this: https://ko-fi.com/mrvolt

A friend gave me a rotary phone mechanism years ago, and I finally got around to turning it into a working cell phone! It can call, text, play FM radio, and store one whole phone number.

-ABS (3D printed on Lulzbot Mini)
-Aluminum
-Brass
-Padouk
-Adafruit Fona Feather (Atmega 32u4 and SIMCOM800L)

-8 ohm 1W speaker

videos.t: Building GLaDOS in Real Life: Part 1
videos.desc:
I'm building a scaled animatronic version of GLaDOS (as she looks in Portal 2). For now, I'm going to be building her head and neck mechanism, but she'll be fully articulated as she is in game. Eventually, I'd love to build her full body, but I'll need a bit more space for that kind of build! 

This is going to be an ongoing project as she's a complicated robot, but that's the fun of the challenge. As she comes along, I'll be adding as many plausible features as I can, but I'm curious to know what you'd like to see her capable of.

If you want to see her come to life, subscribe and let me know

videos.t: Building GLaDOS in Real Life: Part 2
videos.desc:
The second part.

I've made a fair amount of progress on GLaDOS in the past weeks, and now she's got a fully motorized head! Using two new 35Kg.cm servos, she can slide and tilt her eye assembly.

Next time, I'll be adding more head details and creating her neck mechanism. Stay tuned.

videos.t: Building GLaDOS in Real Life: Part 3
videos.desc:
The part where things go perfectly well and everyone is happy :)

Want to buy me a coffee? Your tips support more videos like this: https://ko-fi.com/mrvolt
Support the channel and bigger builds: https://www.patreon.com/mr_volt

Challenges to overcome next time:
Tighten up the tolerances of the joints.
Test microcontroller drive for the servo with smooth acceleration (I'm just using a cheapo servo tester in this video)
Increase clamping force on the main neck rod so GLaDOS can't decapitate herself... again.

videos.t: Building GLaDOS in Real Life: Pt 4
videos.desc:
Been a busy personal month, but I wanted to share a quick update on GLaDOS. I've ordered some linear actuators for her redesigned neck mechanism and will basically be redesigning the entirety of her wall mount.

I'm moving over the next week, so I'll have little time to work, but the next update will share full motion control of her head. Are you excited? I'm excited. Stay safe out there.

videos.t: I made a real working Pokedex
videos.desc:
If you want a custom PCB for your next project, go to https://www.pcbway.com/

Nintendo will never sell an anime accurate Pokedex, so I built my own. My version has a Raspberry Pi Compute module 4, ESP32, Raspberry Pi Pico, advanced SLA 3D printed case, and CNC machined aluminum rear. It can detect Pokemon in photos, has complete entries for all 1000+ existing Pokemon, and has a built in microphone so you can ask it questions about evolutions or moves! 

Hardware design by me. Software by the maestro @BigRigCreates 

Learn more about the Form 4 here: https://formlabs.com/3d-printers/form-4/?ut
